title: A Blue Whale's Heart Beats Just Twice a Minute

scenes.text: A blue whale's heart can beat just twice a minute.
Scientists stuck a heart monitor to one with suction cups in Monterey Bay. Then they listened for nine hours.
Every time it dived for food, its heart slowed to two beats a minute. Back at the surface, it raced up to 37.
In those same sixty seconds, your heart beats about seventy times.
The slow beat saves oxygen on long dives, and the bigger the animal, the slower its heart.
Researchers think that heart is already working at its limit. It may be the reason no animal has ever grown bigger than a blue whale. Could anything ever be bigger?

description:
A blue whale's heart can slow to just two beats per minute.
In 2019 Stanford scientists attached a suction-cup heart monitor to a blue whale in Monterey Bay and recorded nine hours of heartbeats: as low as two beats a minute on feeding dives, and up to 37 at the surface. The team thinks the heart is working near its physical limit, which may explain why no animal has ever evolved to be larger.
Could any animal ever be bigger than a blue whale?
